content:
I opened two PRs that when combined halve the running time (!) of the linting step in Mathlib CI:

  • batteries#2026 runs the linters on a fixed pool of worker threads, instead of one task per check. This reduces contention, and the linters run faster and use less memory.
  • batteries#2028 removes reference-counting work on the environment that the various threads share.

I measured the impact on runLinter Mathlib, on a mathlib CI runner:

Batteries Wall time vs main User CPU System CPU Peak memory
main 273 s 4315 s 663 s 10.6 GiB
batteries#2028 246 s −10% 3595 s 739 s 10.4 GiB
batteries#2026 150 s −45% 4290 s 56 s 7.8 GiB
batteries#2026 + batteries#2028 129 s −53% 3646 s 61 s 7.8 GiB
Still waiting for a review in batteries#2026 which is the more impactful of the two :innocent:
Sorry for the delay, it was mostly waiting on the Mathlib check to clear.
Feel free to ignore, that was some overeager prototyping that didn't amount to much

I was trying to explore some ideas for incrementality but it's hard to fingerprint the environment reliably; heuristics can be "good enough" for PRs but I think it's not worth being incorrect even if you can make it a rare occasion
OK. Make sure to label these WIP.
Oh... they are closed, though, I didn't know the label was the only signal

I meant while they are still open. Once closed, labels should disappear.

When you're exploring ideas, mark the PR as WIP. That's actually better than draft. The best is to do both but then it's easy to forget to undo one.
